# Capability Selection

Load when a requirement needs a logical capability. Expertise grants no authority.

1. Separate reasoning, procedural expertise, executable capability, knowledge,
   control/sequence, context, authority, state, evaluation and observability.
2. Consider the least consequential adequate option:

| Need | Candidate | Does not imply |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Invariant computation | Deterministic code | Model reasoning |
| Relevant background | Instruction/context or retrieval | New agent |
| Procedure within the Golden Path | Supporting reference | Independent skill |
| Demonstrated independent procedural reuse | Skill | Tool permission |
| External execution | Tool/API; MCP if earned | Separate reasoning boundary |
| Interpretation or synthesis | Model reasoning | Autonomous behavior |
| Known sequence | Deterministic control | Model-discovered steps |
| Cross-invocation continuity | Explicit state ownership/retention | Database by default |
| Independent bounded reasoning | Justified subagent/agent | One agent per capability |
| Allowed action | Deterministic authorization/policy | Prompt-only security |
| Consequential judgment | Accountable human review | Autonomous authority |

3. Prefer reuse and simplification. Three MCP servers do not require three agents.
   A technology noun is not a requirement. More composition is not progress.
4. New agent boundaries require execution, context, authority, lifecycle,
   parallelism or control justification. Concurrency also needs independence,
   latency/budget evidence, cancellation, aggregation and failure expectations.
5. Record the capability's governing decision, authority, identity and boundary.
   Derive requirements/workload through its decision. Name omitted components
   and the evidence that would justify reconsideration.

Apply [the Branch Rule](../../../../docs/golden-path.md), including to skill packaging.
